population: Unselected (amyloid-positive early AD or preclinical AD)
note: Four BACE1 inhibitors lowered CSF Aβ in people as dogs and mice predicted, yet none slowed decline and two met unforeseen liver injury.
label: Alzheimer's (BACE1)

engagement.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: LY2886721 Phase 2 (NCT01561430) started March 2012, so the animal PD work predates it; published 2015.
engagement.judgement: Opening year set to the first patient trial of a member drug, as the animal work was unpublished until 2015.
engagement.model: PDAPP mice and cannulated beagle dogs (brain/CSF Aβ)
engagement.note: LY2886721 lowered brain Aβ in PDAPP mice and CSF Aβ ~80% in cannulated dogs before entering patients.
engagement.short: Mice and dogs: CSF/brain Aβ falls
engagement.quote: The in vivo pharmacology properties of LY2886721 were initially tested in the PDAPP mouse, a transgenic mouse expressing a mini-gene for human APP harboring an APP V717F mutation

engagement.magnitude_basis: peak CSF Aβ reduction: dog ~80% vs dose-dependent human reductions described as similar
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6605527). Willis 2022 (doi:10.3233/ADR-210037) repeats the match for LY3202626: dog CSF Aβ ~80% vs human Aβ1-42 −73% at 6 mg. Atabecestat (Timmers 2018) and elenbecestat CSF lowering also held in patients.
engagement.judgement: Aβ is the target's own product, so readout_tier proximal.
engagement.model: PDAPP mice and cannulated beagle dogs (brain/CSF Aβ)
engagement.note: LY2886721 lowered CSF Aβ in healthy volunteers as it had in dogs and mice, in one paper side by side.
engagement.short: Human CSF Aβ fell as in dogs
engagement.quote: Similar potent and persistent amyloid β lowering was observed in plasma and lumbar CSF when single and multiple doses of LY2886721 were administered to healthy human subjects.
engagement.reason: Human CSF Aβ fell as in dogs

dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy (Phase 2 start March 2012).
dose.model: Dog CSF Aβ PK/PD scaled to humans
dose.note: Human doses were chosen to reproduce the CSF Aβ lowering seen in cannulated dogs.
dose.short: Dog CSF PK/PD sets human dose
dose.quote: Central pharmacology studies were conducted in a cannulated beagle dog model established at MPI Research.

dose.magnitude_basis: CSF Aβ reduction at tested human doses vs ~80% in dogs
dose.confidence_note: Full text read. LY2886721 Phase 2 stopped for liver enzymes (no stated margin), which v3 scores untested for dose, so it is not a dose block here.
dose.judgement: Scored the exposure target as reached; adequacy is settled by the efficacy entry that follows.
dose.model: Dog CSF Aβ PK/PD scaled to humans
dose.note: Healthy-volunteer doses reached the dog-level CSF Aβ lowering; whether it was enough was still unknown.
dose.quote: Similar potent and persistent amyloid β lowering was observed in plasma and lumbar CSF when single and multiple doses of LY2886721 were administered to healthy human subjects.

dose.magnitude_basis: PACC change vs placebo at the dose reaching the CSF Aβ target
dose.confidence_note: Full letter read; CSF lowering at 25 mg (~84%) from Sperling 2021 (doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2020.4857). Registry date is NCT02569398 results posting.
dose.judgement: Dose contra derived from the efficacy failure so the failure is counted once; dog PK/PD model is Lilly's, applied across the class.
dose.model: Dog CSF Aβ PK/PD scaled to humans
dose.note: Atabecestat 25 mg (~84% CSF Aβ lowering) reached target yet worsened the primary cognitive endpoint.
dose.quote: At month 6, the difference between the 25-mg group and the placebo group was −1.12 (95% CI, −1.68 to −0.56; P<0.001)

efficacy.confidence_note: Year is a proxy (Phase 2 start March 2012).
efficacy.note: PDAPP mice model Aβ production and plaque, not neuron loss or cognitive decline.
efficacy.quote: The in vivo pharmacology properties of LY2886721 were initially tested in the PDAPP mouse, a transgenic mouse expressing a mini-gene for human APP harboring an APP V717F mutation

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PACC change vs placebo (predicted slowing, observed worsening)
efficacy.confidence_note: Interim analysis of the primary endpoint; final analysis Sperling 2021 confirmed. Model side is brain Aβ lowering in PDAPP mice for LY2886721, a sibling member.
efficacy.judgement: The mouse prediction is implicit (Aβ lowering implies disease modification); paired, not stated. Atabecestat was never tested in the cited mice.
efficacy.note: Atabecestat lowered Aβ as the mice predicted but worsened the primary PACC score in amyloid-positive people.
efficacy.quote: At month 6, the difference between the 25-mg group and the placebo group was −1.12 (95% CI, −1.68 to −0.56; P<0.001)

patient_trials.quote: Atabecestat, 25 mg, showed significant cognitive worsening vs placebo for Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite at month 6

safety.confidence_note: Species of the toxicology studies not stated in the source; year is a proxy.
safety.note: LY2886721 advanced on a toxicology profile free of the retinal pathology that stopped LY2811376.
safety.quote: This robust pharmacology, coupled with a nonclinical toxicology profile without adverse retinal epithelial pathology at pharmacologic doses (as seen previously with LY2811376), led to the advancement of LY2886721 into early phase clinical trials.

safety.magnitude_basis: hepatotoxicity absent in animals, present in patients
safety.population: MCI due to AD or mild AD
safety.confidence_note: Full text read. Willis 2022 states it plainly: 'This finding was not observed in nonclinical toxicology studies'. Lilly announced the stop June 2013 (press release not retrieved). Registry date is NCT01561430 results posting.
safety.judgement: Scored the liver miss as a harm the species could show (mechanism unknown). Atabecestat's immune-mediated, HLA-linked liver injury and the class's reversible cognitive worsening were not scored separately: same status, and their animal predictions were not found.
safety.note: Phase 2 stopped for liver enzyme elevations in 4 of 70 patients; the toxicology studies had not shown it.
safety.quote: Despite the setbacks from unanticipated nonclinical toxicology and clinical AEs experienced with LY2811376 and LY2886721, respectively, which led to the eventual termination of these molecules, the promise of BACE1 inhibitors to test the amyloid hypothesis remains strong.
